subject: BlueHarbor: throughput surge + elevated 5xx — remediation sprint and closure plan
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@blueharbor.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Khatri <samir.k@blueharbor.com>, SRE Team <sre@blueharbor.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Production: large throughput spike -> elevated 5xx and latency (Dec 1)

Vanessa / Redwood team,

We observed a major throughput surge across our production fleet hitting Redwood endpoints between 07:45–08:05 PST. During the window we saw request latency double and 5xx rates increase from baseline ~0.2% to ~4.8%. The incident impacted our customer-facing QA and caused a partial degradation for ~25% of our sessions.

Attached is our snapshot from the BlueHarbor observability layer (throughput_snapshot_20261201.png). Our SRE collected traces that show many requests timing out while being routed to the same inference pool.

Can you confirm whether this was a config/rollout on Redwood's side? We need an initial readout and a plan for mitigation and credits if SLA is impacted. We have a quarterly business review next week and need this on the exec readout.

Appreciate a prompt reply — we are prepared to join a bridge.

— Emily
Emily Zhao
Director, Platform Engineering | BlueHarbor
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@blueharbor.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 08:31:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production: large throughput spike -> elevated 5xx and latency (Dec 1)

Thanks for the heads up, Emily — I’m sorry for the disruption. We’re standing up a short bridge now to triage. I’ve looped Marcus (serving runtime) and Rishi (ops/infra) to provide an initial diagnosis and remediation plan.

Immediate asks from our side:
- Can you share the request IDs (or a small span sample) from 07:45–08:05?
- Any recent traffic pattern changes on your side (batching, parallelization)?

We will aim to provide an initial root cause and mitigation options within 6 hours and a targeted remediation sprint plan within 48 hours. I’ll schedule an exec readout for Fri if that works for your team.

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Success (Strategic Accounts)
Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@blueharbor.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production: large throughput spike -> elevated 5xx and latency (Dec 1)

Quick preliminary triage (from runtime traces and metrics):
- Trigger: a short-lived traffic burst caused a KV-cache eviction race in the prefix cache under continuous batching. The race led to cache misses and repeated rehydration attempts, amplifying token-generation work for a subset of routes.
- Secondary: kernel-selection heuristics on the serving tier picked a higher-latency execution path for long sequences during the burst (likely due to the distribution change), which increased tail latency.
- Autoscale: the autoscaler did not spin up additional fallback capacity fast enough; the scaling threshold is conservative to avoid thrash, but that made the system slower to respond to abrupt bursts.

Mitigations we propose immediately:
1) Apply a hotfix to add a small backoff and single-flight in the KV cache rehydrate path (patch attached: kv-cache-diff.patch). This will be low-risk and roll out in canary first.
2) Temporarily relax autoscale thresholds for BlueHarbor’s reserved pools for the next 72 hours to allow faster ramping.
3) Force a kernel-selection fallback for long sequences for the next 24 hours to reduce tail latency.
4) Create a bridging route that directs at-risk requests to a pre-warmed fallback pool.

Owner assignments (initial):
- Marcus: patch rollout and kernel fallback (ETA: 3 hours to canary, 8 hours to full if canary is clean)
- Rishi: autoscale policy tweak and fallback pool provisioning (ETA: 2 hours to confirm capacity)
- Laura: customer communications and exec readout coordination (ETA: schedule within 24 hrs)

I’ll attach the metrics snapshot and a minimal patch for the cache bug. We’ll coordinate the canary window with BlueHarbor on the bridge.

— Marcus
Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Production: large throughput spike -> elevated 5xx and latency (Dec 1)

Thanks Marcus — that aligns with some of the traces we have. Two asks for the near term:
1) We need an exec-level readout deck for Friday morning PST with: timeline, customer impact (sessions affected), root cause summary, and the remediation plan + exact ETA for mitigating the issue.
2) Please confirm whether BlueHarbor is eligible for SLA credits for the incident window; our procurement team will flag this as part of the billing review.

Samir (cc) will coordinate procurement questions. We will stand by for the canary and status updates.

— Emily
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@blueharbor.com>, Samir Khatri <samir.k@blueharbor.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 09:00:00 -08:00
Subject: BlueHarbor remediation sprint plan + action tracker (readout attached)

Emily / Samir — attaching the remediation sprint board and an executive readout link. Summary below — full deck in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/BlueHarbor+Post-Incident+Readout

Executive summary:
- Root cause: KV-cache eviction race under burst + kernel-selection tail-path for long sequences.
- Customer impact: estimated 22% of sessions experienced increased latency or transient 5xx between 07:45–08:05 PST on 2026-12-01. We estimate ~0.8% of total API calls retried by clients.
- Action plan: 48-hour remediation sprint (hotfix -> canary -> rollback plan), autoscale policy relaxation for 72 hours, and pre-warmed fallback pool for APs.
- Timeline & owners: see attached remediation_sprint_board.csv.
- SLA credits: pending final impact calculation; legal/procurement will receive a draft credit calculation by EOD Monday — we will route the formal proposal via DocuSign if accepted.

Immediate asks from BlueHarbor for sign-off:
- Approve temporary autoscale relaxation for reserved pools (72 hours).
- Confirm a 60-minute canary window starting today at 10:30 PST.

If we get approvals, Marcus will kick off the canary at 10:30 and Rishi will post capacity confirmation by 10:15. Laura will run the exec readout on Friday at 11:00 PST.

Attachments: remediation_sprint_board.csv, throughput_snapshot_20261201.png

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Success (Strategic Accounts)
Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@blueharbor.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Dec 2026 17:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: BlueHarbor remediation sprint plan + action tracker (readout attached)

Quick update following the sprint and the readout: canary completed cleanly (10:30–11:30 PST), hotfix applied to canary and promoted after a 30-minute observation window. Autoscale thresholds relaxed; fallback pool pre-warmed and healthy.

Next steps I own:
- Runbook updates for cache single-flight pattern (ETA: 3 days).
- Autoscale policy change to be templated and added to governance (ETA: 2 weeks).
- Post-incident QA: coord with BlueHarbor SRE to validate long-tail sequences across peak traffic windows (ETA: 1 week).

Vanessa — please confirm whether BlueHarbor wants the formal SLA credit calculation to be transmitted now; Marcus & I will attach final metrics and the impact calculation.

Thanks everyone — closing the immediate remediation loop; we’ll keep the weekly sync until the governance changes are in place.

— Rishi
Head of Infra Ops
Redwood Inference
